flagged.title: The Inspector's Role
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly attributes Sheila Birling's famous quote ('these girls aren't cheap labour, they're people') directly to Inspector Goole, which is a penalised factual error in GCSE English Literature.

mark_affecting.video_says: When the Inspector says: 'these girls aren't cheap labour, they're people', that is J.B. Priestley himself talking.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: When he tells Sheila that factories always know where to look for 'cheap labour', she answers him — 'these girls aren’t cheap labour — they’re people'

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly teaches Eduqas GCSE students that AO4 assesses historical context, whereas on this specification AO4 assesses SPaG (accurate written English) and context is not assessed on this paper.

mark_affecting.video_says: and AO4 for that crucial historical context
mark_affecting.lesson_says: It tests AO1 (understanding and response), AO2 (analysis of language, form and structure) and AO4, which rewards accurate written English. Context is not assessed on this question.

mark_affecting.video_says: And let's not forget our golden rule for AO4 context. AO4 is all about showing how the 1912 setting of the play and the 1945 reality of the audience actually impact the scene.
